title: Fixed-degree pseudo-coherence under the affine derived equivalence
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $m\in\mathbf Z$, and $M\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\widetilde M\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$ be the image of $M$ under the equivalence of [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence], induced by associating a quasi-coherent sheaf termwise to a representative complex [def-pc-derived-category]. Then $\widetilde M$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent on $Y$ [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] if and only if $M$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent as an object of $D(A)$ [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. There is no Noetherian hypothesis and no boundedness assumption on a representative of $M$.

proof.text: Write F_B for the affine equivalence over a commutative ring B. By [new-affine-derived-tilde-homology-comparison], naturally in a derived morphism u, H^j(F_B(u)) is the associated-sheaf map of H^j(u). The associated-sheaf functor is fully faithful by parts (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], and preserves cokernels by part (4). Thus it preserves and reflects isomorphisms and surjections: preservation of surjections follows by applying it to a zero cokernel; for reflection, if v,w agree after a module map h whose associated-sheaf map is epic, their associated-sheaf maps agree by cancellation, hence v=w by faithfulness. This tests exactly categorical epimorphisms, which for modules are surjections. Consequently F_B preserves and reflects the cohomological conditions in degrees j>m and j=m, for arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Tag 06Z0, lemma-affine-compare-bounded, cohomology calculation; Tag 08E7, both implications

proof.text: Suppose M is m-pseudo-coherent. Unpack [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent] to obtain a bounded finite free complex E and a derived map u:Q(E)\to M with the required cohomology isomorphisms and surjection. Apply [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] to u. Its source is Q(\widetilde E). The associated sheaf of A is the structure sheaf (apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] with N=A); preservation of finite direct sums in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](4) identifies the terms of \widetilde E with finite free sheaves. It is zero outside the same finite interval, hence strictly perfect by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Step 1 gives the required cohomology conditions. The single open Y and this map therefore witness [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 08E7, lemma-pseudo-coherent-affine, first sentence of proof

proof.text: For the converse choose a representative complex N of M. The affine equivalence identifies \widetilde M with Q(\widetilde N). For each x\in Y, [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] supplies an open W\ni x, a strictly perfect complex P on W, and a derived map \alpha:Q(P)\to Q(\widetilde N)|_W inducing isomorphisms above m and a surjection at m. Its terms are retracts of finite free sheaves and vanish outside a finite interval, by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Apply [lem-pc-finite-retract-sheaves-affine-trivialization] to the finite set of degrees in that interval: there is an affine V\ni x inside W on which all its nonzero terms become finite free simultaneously. Terms outside the interval are already zero and free of rank zero.

source.place: Tag 08E7, converse: local strictly perfect approximations and refinement making their finitely many terms free

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i) choose f_x with x\in D(f_x)\subseteq V. Restrict P and \alpha further to D(f_x). Restriction preserves kernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-limits] and cokernels by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1), so it preserves the quotient ker(d^j)/im(d^{j-1}) defining H^j; for an open inclusion j:W'\to W one has j^{-1}\mathcal O_W=\mathcal O_{W'}, so by [def-pc-derived-pullback] Lj^* is termwise restriction of a K-flat resolution \mathcal P^\bullet\to E; restriction is exact, so j^{-1}\mathcal P^\bullet\to j^{-1}E is a quasi-isomorphism and Lj^*E is the termwise restriction of E, compatibly with composing the restrictions Y\supseteq W\supseteq D(f_x). Thus the restricted map still has the same cohomology conditions. Restricting a finite free sheaf gives a finite free sheaf, by restricting its finite tuple sections; the finite degree interval is unchanged. All such D(f_x) cover Y. Quasi-compactness in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](iii) gives a finite subcover D(f_1),\ldots,D(f_r), and part (i) says (f_1,\ldots,f_r)=A.

source.place: Tag 08E7, converse: finite standard-open refinement; restriction computation using Tags 01AH, 01AJ

proof.text: Fix one member D(f_i) of this finite cover and put B=A_{f_i}. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] it is the open subscheme Spec(B) with its structure sheaf. We can therefore regard the restricted bounded finite free complex P_i and its approximation map as living on Spec(B). The target Q(\widetilde N)|_{D(f_i)} is canonically Q(\widetilde{N\otimes_A B}). Explicitly, on the basis of opens D(g/1) of Spec(B) (every element of B is g/f_i^a and f_i is a unit), its degree-n sections are (N^n)_{f_i g} by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections]; the associated sheaf of N^n\otimes_A B has those same modules, with n/f_i^a mapped to the identical fraction. The restriction maps agree by that node's restriction formula. These maps and their inverses glue on the basis, commute with differentials by functoriality in module maps, and give the asserted isomorphism of complexes. This is a comparison of actual complexes, hence also an isomorphism in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 08E7, local affine module identification; Tags 01HV (sections and restrictions), 01I3 (standard open affine)

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-affine-finite-free-sheaf-complex-lift] over B to P_i. It gives a bounded-above finite free module complex E_i and an actual complex isomorphism \widetilde E_i\simeq P_i. It is also bounded below: outside the finite degree interval of P_i, \widetilde{E_i^j}=0, so E_i^j=0 because E_i^j\simeq\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\widetilde{E_i^j}) by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](2). If literal zero terms are desired, replace these zero objects by the zero module and conjugate differentials through the degreewise isomorphisms. Now compose the derived image of this complex isomorphism with the map of Step 5. Fullness of the affine equivalence [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] over B gives a derived map Q(E_i)\to Q(N\otimes_A B) whose image is that composite. Both endpoints have quasi-coherent cohomology, so the map belongs to the full subcategory D_QCoh. Step 1 reflects its cohomology isomorphisms above m and surjection at m. The bounded finite free E_i and this map witness m-pseudo-coherence of Q(N\otimes_A B) by [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent]. No chain-map representative of this derived map is needed.

source.place: Tag 08E7, converse: finite free affine approximations; Tag 06Z0 for fullness on derived morphisms

proof.text: For every i, Step 6 gives m-pseudo-coherence of the localized representative N\otimes_A A_{f_i}, and Step 4 gives the unit ideal condition. Apply the fixed-m clause of [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-localization-glue] to conclude that N, hence M, is m-pseudo-coherent. This uses the fixed degree m throughout, not an assertion for all m. If A is the zero ring, Y is empty and D(A) is the zero category; the zero complex and the unique map give the ring-side witness and the empty covering gives the sheaf-side witness. The argument for nonempty Y uses boundedness only of the approximating P_i and E_i, never of N; no Noetherian hypothesis occurs.

Steps 2,5 identify the structure sheaf and restriction to a principal open by the specified fraction maps.
Step 3 trivializes all finitely many nonzero approximation terms on a common neighbourhood; this does not assert pseudo-coherence.
Steps 4,5 need the standard-open basis and its localization-spectrum description.
Step 4 needs kernel preservation for exact restriction of module sheaves.
Step 4 needs cokernel preservation for exact restriction of module sheaves.
Step 4 needs a finite standard subcover and the unit-ideal condition.
Step 5 needs Spec(A_f) identified with D(f) as an open subscheme, including its structure sheaf.
Step 6 needs an actual complex isomorphism lifting the finite free sheaf approximant; lower boundedness is then proved explicitly.
Step 7 uses the fixed-m ring gluing theorem, the algebraic tool expressly invoked by 08E7.
